prompt: Postcranial skeletal pneumaticity (PSP) refers to the presence of extensions of an animal's lungs and air sacs inside its bones. These extensions are known as pneumatic diverticula. <u>Vascularity and other identifying characteristics of pneumatic diverticula tend not to fossilize, so paleontologists have relied on studies of living bird species to document these qualities,</u> augmenting their findings from fossil analysis to glean additional insights into the respiratory systems of extinct genera such as Tyrannosaurus, Euhelopus, and other Cretaceous theropods and sauropods that may have also exhibited PSP.
question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined portion in the text as a whole?

options.A: It presents information about the fossilization of pneumatic diverticula that has led paleontologists to question the applicability of studies of certain living species.
options.B: It accounts for disagreements among paleontologists about how the respiratory systems of certain extinct genera functioned.
options.C: It highlights an issue with fossils that previously led paleontologists to misidentify certain characteristics of pneumatic diverticula.
options.D: It indicates why paleontologists have used another approach in addition to fossil analysis to learn about certain aspects of pneumatic diverticula.

prompt: Cardiff, Wales, has installed engineered structures—mainly breakwalls—along 87% of its shoreline to protect infrastructure from storm surges and other hazards, a practice known as shoreline hardening. Investigating the impact of such structures on waterbird communities at various sites in the Chesapeake Bay on the US East Coast, Diann Prosser et al. hypothesized that shoreline hardening more negatively affects waterbirds than does land development for uses such as housing or agriculture. To evaluate the responses of local waterbird species, including the osprey, to landscape alterations, the researchers utilized the Index of Waterbird Community Integrity (IWCI), on which a low score corresponds to low community integrity.
question: Which finding, if true, would most directly support the researchers' hypothesis?

options.A: Waterbird communities at Back River, a site with a relatively high percentage of developed land and a relatively low percentage of hardened shoreline, had higher average IWCI scores than did waterbird communities at Magothy, a site with a lower percentage of developed land but a higher percentage of hardened shoreline.
options.B: Waterbird communities at Langford, a site with a relatively high percentage of developed land and a relatively high percentage of hardened shoreline, had lower average IWCI scores than did waterbird communities at Mill Seat, a site with a lower percentage of developed land but a higher percentage of hardened shoreline.
options.C: Waterbird communities at Stony and Curtis, two sites with relatively high percentages of developed land and hardened shorelines, had similar IWCI scores, whereas waterbird communities at Ware and Iongo, two sites with relatively low percentages of developed land and hardened shorelines, had widely differing IWCI scores.
options.D: Waterbird communities at Old Road, a site with a relatively high percentage of developed land and hardened shoreline, had lower average IWCI scores than did waterbird communities at Quantock, a site with a relatively low percentage of developed land and hardened shoreline.

prompt:
Ranking of Environmental and Sociocultural Benefits of Urban Agriculture (scale of 1 to 25; 1 = highest)

| Social or ecological service | Project leaders | Stakeholders | General public |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| improvement of social cohesion | 17 | 10 | 9 |
| prevention of soil erosion | 13 | 11 | 23 |
| conservation of genetic variability | 5 | 18 | 16 |
| improvement of urban aesthetics and art inspiration | 8 | 4 | 6 |
| enhancement of pollination | 1 | 7 | 12 |

Esther Sanyé-Mengual, Kathrin Specht, and their team surveyed three groups of people in Bologna, Italy to compare their views about the extent to which urban agriculture contributes to 25 services. Using only the rankings shown in the table, a city planner in Bologna who is promoting a new urban agriculture project concludes that advertisements aimed at project leaders should emphasize the project's benefit to the enhancement of pollination.
question: Which choice best describes data in the table that support the city planner's conclusion?

options.A: The conservation of genetic variability was ranked lower for project leaders than it was for the general public.
options.B: The enhancement of pollination was ranked higher for project leaders than it was for stakeholders.
options.C: The enhancement of pollination was ranked higher for project leaders than were the other four services.
options.D: The improvement of social cohesion was ranked higher for project leaders than was the enhancement of pollination.

prompt: Mooseberry (Viburnum edule) plants are native to Alaska, where harsh conditions have historically impeded potential invasive species. As the boreal climate has warmed in recent decades, however, common knotgrass (Polygonum aviculare) plants have established themselves in Alaska. It has been suggested that warming-induced delays in the onset of subfreezing temperatures in autumn can benefit invasives more than native species; to evaluate this possibility, biologists Christa Mulder and Katie Spellman tracked V. edule and P. aviculare, concluding that invasives are advantaged by delays in subfreezing temperature onset in Alaska.
question: Which finding, if true, would most directly support Mulder and Spellman's conclusion?

options.A: Although V. edule and P. aviculare both tended to produce leaves later into autumn in years with late subfreezing temperature onset, the extension was much greater for P. aviculare than for V. edule.
options.B: Although significant interannual variations in subfreezing temperature onset were observed during the study, neither P. aviculare nor V. edule showed any significant interannual variation in the cessation of leaf production.
options.C: Although V. edule and P. aviculare tended to stop producing leaves at about the same time in years with historically typical temperature patterns, P. aviculare stopped producing leaves sooner than V. edule did in years with late subfreezing temperature onset.
options.D: Although V. edule and P. aviculare both tended to produce more leaves overall in years with late subfreezing temperature onset than they did in years with historically typical temperature patterns, the years with late subfreezing temperature onset also had early growing season onset in spring.

explanation: Loài xâm lấn P. aviculare kéo dài thời gian mọc lá vào mùa thu nhiều hơn hẳn so với loài bản địa khi mùa đông đến muộn, tạo lợi thế sinh trưởng rõ rệt.

prompt: In June of 1988, Morocco liberalized its stock market, meaning that it began allowing foreign individuals and businesses to invest money in Moroccan companies. This was part of a wave of stock market liberalizations around the world—Argentina in 1989, Jamaica in 1991, and so on. The standard view among economists at the time was that liberalization would make it easier for companies to raise money from investors. Economist Peter Blair Henry examined the economies of 11 countries that were part of the liberalization wave and found that, on average, companies based in those countries received significant increases in investment in the three years following liberalization, suggesting that __________
question: Which choice most logically completes the text?

options.A: companies in the countries Henry studied did not benefit from liberalization until at least three years after liberalization occurred.
options.B: companies in Argentina experienced a greater increase in investment following liberalization than did companies in Morocco.
options.C: economists who held the standard view of liberalization failed to anticipate some serious negative effects of liberalization.
options.D: economists' expectations about the effect of liberalization on investment were largely correct for the countries Henry studied.

explanation: Dữ liệu thực tế cho thấy lượng vốn đầu tư tăng mạnh đúng như kỳ vọng ban đầu của các nhà kinh tế học.

prompt: Anthropogenic noise (sounds from human sources like traffic or mining) can affect animals, as Alvin Aaden Yim-Hol Chan and colleagues found in a 2010 study of Caribbean hermit crabs. A meta-analysis of more than 100 such studies examining various species found that, for every study, relevant traits or behaviors of the animals were observably different between the exposed group and the otherwise similar but unexposed group, regardless of whether that difference was beneficial or detrimental for the exposed group. So while a study of birds might show a difference that benefits the exposed group, and a study of arthropods might show a difference that's harmful to the exposed group, both differences are substantial. Therefore, the results of the meta-analysis suggest that __________
question: Which choice most logically completes the text?

options.A: the studies in the meta-analysis that examined arthropods were more likely than those about birds to specify whether the observed effects were detrimental.
options.B: the studies of the birds likely found significantly larger effects of exposure to anthropogenic noise than most studies of arthropods except the study of Caribbean hermit crabs by Alvin Aaden Yim-Hol Chan and colleagues.
options.C: exposure to anthropogenic noise will likely have noticeable effects both on arthropods such as Caribbean hermit crabs and on birds such as reed buntings, but the nature of that effect could be very different for the two species.
options.D: the study conducted by Alvin Aaden Yim-Hol Chan and colleagues found substantial differences, but studies included in the meta-analysis of arthropods other than Caribbean hermit crabs likely did not.

prompt: The Clouds is a 423 BCE play by Aristophanes, originally written in ancient Greek. At the time, professional intellectuals called sophists taught customers rhetorical techniques to use in public speaking, along with providing instruction in other subjects. In the play, Aristophanes suggests that the teachings of sophists are a danger to civic order, as seen when the character __________
question: Which choice most effectively uses a quotation from a translation of The Clouds to illustrate the claim?

options.A: Socrates, a sophist, says to a potential customer, 'Is the power of speaking, pray, implanted in your nature?'
options.B: Pheidippides says, after taking lessons from a sophist, 'How pleasant it is to be acquainted with new and clever things, and to be able to despise the established laws!'
options.C: Strepsiades encourages his son to learn to be a sophist, saying, 'Go, I entreat you, dearest of men, go and be taught.'
options.D: Strepsiades says of a sophist business, 'This is a thinking-shop of wise spirits. There dwell men who in speaking of the heavens persuade people that it is an oven, and that it encompasses us, and that we are the embers.'

explanation: Câu nói của Pheidippides ('thật thú vị khi có thể khinh thường các luật lệ đã được ban hành') thể hiện trực tiếp mối đe dọa đối với trật tự công dân.

prompt: All stainless steel contains varying amounts of iron, carbon, and corrosion-inhibiting chromium. However, ferritic stainless steel, often used for induction cookers, contains a higher percentage of chromium (at least 10.5%) than does austenitic stainless steel and a higher concentration of iron, which is responsible for its magnetic properties. Unlike ferritic stainless steel, austenitic stainless steel has a face-centered cubic crystalline structure resulting from the addition of nickel to the alloy. Austenitic stainless steel has two subtypes: the 200 series, often used for home water tanks, and the 300 series, which has more nickel than the 200 series and is often used for storage containers or sinks. Thus, stainless steel used to manufacture __________
question: Which choice most logically completes the text?

options.A: induction cookers will have a face-centered cubic crystalline structure.
options.B: home water tanks will have a lower percentage of chromium in its composition than stainless steel used for induction cookers will.
options.C: storage containers will have a concentration of chromium lower than 10.5%, while stainless steel used to manufacture home water tanks will not.
options.D: sinks will have similar magnetic properties to stainless steel used to manufacture induction cookers.

explanation: Thép dùng cho bình nước gia đình thuộc nhóm austenitic, vốn có tỷ lệ crom thấp hơn nhóm ferritic (dùng cho bếp từ).

prompt: Livelihoods for scholars during the Enlightenment were frequently __________, though inheriting a large estate while young probably gave René Descartes a base that assisted his attempts at writing Meditations, Discourse on Method, plus various treatises currently studied.
question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
explanation: 'Precarious' (bấp bênh, không ổn định) tương phản với nền tảng tài chính vững chắc nhờ thừa kế điền trang của Descartes.

prompt: An extreme focus on cases of star formation, such as the beginning of the Pillars of Creation, leads to a discovery-based lean that __________ research in observational astronomy. Examining cosmic decay (like the cooling of planetary nebulae over millions of years) is therefore a vital fix for the popular notion that all bright objects in the sky remain permanent and unchanging.
question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
explanation: 'Pervades' (lan tỏa, tràn ngập khắp nơi) mô tả khuynh hướng thịnh hành chi phối hầu hết các nghiên cứu thiên văn quan sát.

prompt: Theater and film scholars often draw parallels between the lives of performers and aspects of roles they've played; however, the most insightful of these discussions, such as Linda Costanzo Cahir's consideration of resemblances between actor Vivien Leigh and the character Blanche DuBois, maintain a rigid distinction between the actor and the character, taking care never to __________ them.
question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
explanation: 'Conflate' (đánh đồng, trộn lẫn làm một) tương phản với việc 'duy trì sự phân biệt rạch ròi' (rigid distinction).

prompt: The Art Institute of Chicago houses nearly 300,000 works from around the world. Museum visitors looking to __________ their art-viewing experience should turn to Chicago's streets, where they can find works ranging from Joan Miró's sculpture Miró's Chicago at Brunswick Plaza to Kristen Kula's mural Tornado on East 11th Street.
question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
explanation: 'Supplement' (bổ sung, làm phong phú thêm) cho trải nghiệm ngắm nghệ thuật trong bảo tàng bằng các tác phẩm ngoài đường phố.

prompt: Mauricio Drelichman and Hans-Joachim Voth's analysis of the debt repayments and expenditure of the government of Philip II (who ruled an empire including Spain and Milan from 1556 to 1598) found a seeming contradiction: although the government had several short-term cash shortages, it ran an even larger surplus than did the government of eighteenth-century Britain, a nation considered __________ of fiscal virtue.
question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
explanation: 'An exemplar' (tấm gương mẫu mực, hình mẫu điển hình) về kỷ luật tài khóa.

prompt: The __________ of prose structures in global fiction nowadays indicates the narrative perks of the realist novel that grew through commercial printing and mass marketing during the eighteenth century. This literary mode expanded swiftly and widely, fully ousting regional storytelling customs in areas such as remote Scotland and rural Russia by the conclusion of the nineteenth century.
question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
explanation: 'Omnipresence' (sự hiện diện khắp mọi nơi) mô tả việc thể loại tiểu thuyết hiện thực lan tỏa và chiếm lĩnh văn đàn toàn cầu.

prompt: Some ethicists challenge the concept of personal character, claiming that if it were meaningful, situational factors could not, as they clearly can, induce behavior contrary to that character. As Rachana Kamtekar observes, this argument is difficult to reconcile with our lay conception of character: we expect a person of helpful character to be frequently helpful, not __________ helpful.
question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
explanation: 'Unfailingly' (luôn luôn, không một lần sai sót) đối chiếu với quan niệm thông thường rằng một người tốt tính chỉ cần 'frequently helpful' chứ không nhất thiết lúc nào cũng hoàn hảo không tì vết.

prompt: Statistical modeling of entire populations and other generalized frameworks permit biologists to identify wide trends, yet these techniques __________ the distinct characteristics of single organisms. By investigating specific specimens and behaviors in thorough depth, specialized case reports and other focused studies endeavor to reveal how larger environmental changes are felt by one creature.
question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
explanation: 'Expunge' (xóa bỏ, triệt tiêu) phản ánh nhược điểm của mô hình thống kê tổng quát khi nó làm mờ đi/loại bỏ các đặc tính riêng lẻ của từng cá thể.

prompt: The subscription model in which consumers who do not deliberately cancel their subscriptions automatically pay recurring fees for access to products and services benefits retailers when consumer passivity is high. Many of the 8.5 percent of subscribers who canceled their food and beverage subscriptions in January 2022 had stopped valuing their subscriptions long before then, but sellers profited from these customers' __________ in the interim.
question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
explanation: 'Inertia' (sự trì trệ, thụ động không hành động) khớp với cụm 'consumer passivity' phía trước.

prompt: Containing over 160 billion base pairs of DNA resulting from polyploidy (whole genome duplication) and accumulation of noncoding DNA without significant deletion, the genome of Tmesipteris oblanceolata (New Caledonian fork fern) is the largest known among eukaryotes—and, given the high biological costs of extremely large genomes, is unlikely to be __________
question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
explanation: 'Supplanted' (bị thay thế, bị soán ngôi) mang nghĩa kỷ lục về kích thước bộ gen của loài dương xỉ này khó lòng bị vượt qua bởi sinh vật khác.

prompt: An effort to raise the toll that drivers must pay to use the Teodoro Moscoso Bridge, which spans the San José Lagoon in Puerto Rico, should explain why a higher toll is necessary; no amount of justification, however, is likely to persuade some drivers who believe the current toll is __________
question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
explanation: 'Exorbitant' (quá cao, cắt cổ) phù hợp với ngữ cảnh những tài xế phản đối tăng phí vì cho rằng mức phí hiện tại vốn đã quá đắt đỏ.

prompt:
The following text is from Yung Wing's 1909 memoir My Life in China and America. Yung Wing was the first person from China to graduate from a US university.

Little did I realize when in 1845 I wrote, while in the Morrison School, a composition on "An Imaginary Voyage to New York and the Hudson," that I was to see New York in reality. <u>This incident leads me to the reflection that sometimes our imagination foreshadows what lies uppermost in our minds and brings possibilities within the sphere of realities.</u>
question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?

options.A: It foreshadows Yung's future difficulties in publishing his writings.
options.B: It describes an event in Yung's life that exemplifies a phenomenon.
options.C: It indicates Yung's unwillingness to distinguish between reality and fantasy as a child.
options.D: It illustrates the role that education played in Yung's childhood.

prompt: Arthur Conan Doyle, the author of the 1902 novel The Hound of the Baskervilles and dozens of other stories featuring the detective Sherlock Holmes, hoped to be remembered chiefly for his historical novels. Although he completed many such works, including The White Company (1891), he became world-famous instead as the creator of Holmes, the character still most closely associated with his name. A student researching popular fiction asserts that <u>even though Doyle grew weary of the character, he ultimately yielded to readers' desire for more Holmes stories.</u>
question: Which statement, if true, would best illustrate the student's claim in the underlined text?

options.A: Doyle had Holmes plunge to his apparent death in an 1893 story in order to free himself to write other kinds of fiction.
options.B: Doyle based Holmes's powers of deduction partly on those of Joseph Bell, a physician who had taught him at the University of Edinburgh.
options.C: Doyle regarded The White Company as one of his finest achievements, even though it is far less widely read today than his Holmes stories.
options.D: After killing off Holmes in 1893 to focus on other writing, Doyle revived the detective a decade later in response to persistent appeals from readers.

explanation: Dữ kiện Doyle 'hồi sinh' Holmes sau một thập kỷ do độc giả liên tục khẩn khoản yêu cầu minh họa trực tiếp cho việc ông đã nhượng bộ trước mong muốn của công chúng.

prompt: Hydrologists recently developed a model to forecast how growing water demand will affect streamflow in river basins in the western United States. Unfortunately, when the model is applied to basins fed mainly by melting snowpack, its forecasts of spring streamflow are too low, and when it is applied to basins fed mainly by rainfall, its forecasts of summer streamflow are too high. The Yampa River basin in northwestern Colorado receives most of its water from snowmelt. If used to forecast the effect of growing water demand on the Yampa River basin over the next decade, the model would therefore likely __________
question: Which choice most logically completes the text?

options.A: overestimate the basin's actual summer streamflow.
options.B: underestimate the basin's actual spring streamflow.
options.C: exaggerate the effect of growing water demand on rainfall-fed tributaries.
options.D: account for factors affecting streamflow other than growing water demand.

explanation: Vì lưu vực sông Yampa nhận nước chủ yếu từ tuyết tan, mô hình sẽ dự báo dòng chảy mùa xuân quá thấp (underestimate the actual spring streamflow).

prompt: With an average summer temperature of 67.7 degrees Fahrenheit, Budapest is one European __________ many travelers recommend, especially from June to September.
question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation: Mệnh đề quan hệ xác định dùng đại từ 'that' và không dùng dấu phẩy đi trước.

prompt: In their 2019 study of butterfly diversity at Rupa Lake in Nepal, researcher Bijaya Neupane and his colleagues counted one bluetail jester __________ to the Nymphalidae family, the bluetail jester (Symbrenthia niphanda) is known to be very rare.
question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation: Dấu chấm phân tách hai mệnh đề độc lập. Mệnh đề sau bắt đầu bằng cụm phân từ: 'Belonging to the Nymphalidae family, the bluetail jester...'.

prompt: Isotopic analysis of tooth enamel from the grave of the Amesbury Archer, a man buried near Stonehenge around 2300 BCE, has revealed striking evidence of long-distance travel in prehistoric Europe, the oxygen isotope ratios __________ that he spent his childhood in a colder region of central Europe, possibly near the Alps.
question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation: Cấu trúc tuyệt đối độc lập dùng phân từ hiện tại 'suggesting' nối tiếp bổ nghĩa cho mệnh đề trước.

prompt: As a massive ice sheet advances, its enormous weight presses the underlying crust downward, displacing some of the mantle beneath it. __________, the crust just beyond the ice sheet's margins is pushed slightly upward, forming a broad ridge that geologists call a peripheral bulge.
question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
explanation: 'Simultaneously' (đồng thời) diễn tả hành động vỏ trái đất ở rìa bị đẩy trồi lên xảy ra cùng lúc với quá trình tảng băng đè lún vùng trung tâm.

prompt: Researchers in France claim that leopards and brown bears are among the twenty most 'charismatic' animals (defined as 'attractive, fascinating, or appealing'). To create their top-twenty list, researchers used survey data from Western Europe. European attitudes toward leopards and brown bears might not be shared around the world, __________
question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
explanation: 'Of course' dùng để thừa nhận một sự thật hiển nhiên (thị hiếu ở Tây Âu dĩ nhiên có thể không đại diện cho toàn thế giới).

prompt: In 1970, Maggie Kuhn had to retire from her job as a secretary because the organization she worked for had a mandatory retirement age of sixty-five. Kuhn noted that since her capabilities did not change when she turned sixty-five, such a policy was entirely __________. This observation prompted her to become an advocate for the rights of older people in the United States.
question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
explanation: 'Arbitrary' (tùy tiện, cảm tính) diễn tả chính sách áp đặt tuổi hưu mà không dựa trên năng lực thực tế.

prompt: Marine ecologist Priya Natarajan and colleagues __________ aquarium tanks with communities of burrowing invertebrates collected from four estuaries along the Gulf of Maine, including sites dominated by mudflats and by salt marsh. The team then planted eelgrass seedlings in the tanks to determine whether the different invertebrate communities affected the seedlings' root growth.
question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
explanation: 'Stocked' nghĩa là thả sinh vật hoặc cung cấp nguồn mẫu sống vào bể thí nghiệm.

prompt: Sperm whales communicate using rapid sequences of sharp, broadband clicks called codas, which differ markedly from the long, low-frequency moans typical of baleen whales. Because these clicks can be readily __________ the calls of other whale species sharing the same waters, researchers using relatively simple underwater microphones have been able to monitor sperm whale groups even in areas where many whale species congregate.
question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
explanation: 'Discerned from' (phân biệt được với) lý giải vì sao các nhà nghiên cứu dễ dàng nhận diện cá voi nhà táng giữa nhiều loài cá voi khác.

prompt: Recent performances reconstructing the music of ancient Greece, such as those organized by classicist Armand D'Angour, are notable for the __________ of the scholarship behind them: the researchers consulted surviving fragments of musical notation, ancient treatises on rhythm and tuning, and replicas of excavated instruments such as the aulos to make the performances as historically accurate as possible.
question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
explanation: 'Exhaustiveness' (sự thấu đáo, toàn diện, tỉ mỉ) phù hợp với việc nhóm nghiên cứu tham khảo từ tàn tích bản nhạc, tài liệu cổ đến phục dựng nhạc cụ.

prompt: Microwave heating, a thermal technology used to preserve food on an industrial scale, is generally considered to be an improvement over more conventional thermal preservation methods. Scientists in Latin America have contributed to a better understanding of this technology, with researchers from Brazil demonstrating its effectiveness in preserving mango peels. As research continues, scientists hope to make advancements in hybrid systems combining multiple food preservation technologies, which would be advantageous over using microwave heating alone, <u>given that it often heats food unevenly.</u>
question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined portion in the text as a whole?

prompt: A team of urban planners in Tucson, Arizona, is designing a network of protected bike lanes for a neighborhood that currently has none. A researcher has argued that the survey no longer accurately reflects the attitudes of the neighborhood's current residents.
question: Which finding, if true, would most directly support the researcher's claim?

options.A: Residents of Tucson are much less likely to bicycle on summer afternoons than on winter mornings.

prompt: Rafael Núñez and colleagues studied how members of the Yupno, an Indigenous group in Papua New Guinea, conceptualize time in both spoken language and gestures. question: Which finding, if true, would most directly support Núñez and colleagues' claim?

options.A: Some Yupno grammatical structures used when talking about time are also used in Hebrew.
options.B: Yupno speakers typically use their left hands to make temporal gestures regardless of whether the gestures are past oriented or future oriented.

prompt: Municipal water utilities in drought-prone regions—including many in California, where a severe drought from 2012 to 2016 depleted reservoirs—often struggle to meet demand during extended dry periods. prompt: Volcanoes are often classified into three main types: shield volcanoes, stratovolcanoes, and cinder cones. Mauna Loa in Hawai'i is a shield volcano, for __________ an estimated volume of about 75,000 km³, it is also the largest active volcano on Earth.

prompt: The formation of desert varnish—the dark coating found on exposed rocks in arid regions—is an exceptionally slow process, the coating typically __________ by only a few micrometers every thousand years as windblown clay particles and manganese oxides build up on rock surfaces.

prompt: The Code of Hammurabi was one of the first written sets of laws and was surprisingly detailed for its time. __________ it contained almost 300 different rules covering everything from business dealings to family matters for the people of Babylon.

prompt: Whereas most flowering plants produce seeds only after their egg cells are fertilized by pollen, the common dandelion (Taraxacum officinale) is largely apomictic; __________ it produces viable seeds without fertilization, so each seed is genetically identical to the parent plant.
question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
explanation: 'That is,' (tức là) giải thích trực tiếp khái niệm apomictic (sinh sản vô tính qua hạt không cần thụ phấn).

prompt: For 130 years, the kilogram was defined by a physical object: a platinum-iridium cylinder stored in a vault near Paris, against which the world's standard masses were periodically compared. __________ the meter has been defined since 1983 not by any object but by the distance light travels in a vacuum during a specified fraction of a second.
question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
explanation: 'By contrast,' tương phản giữa đơn vị kg (từng định nghĩa bằng vật thể thực) và đơn vị mét (được định nghĩa bằng hằng số ánh sáng).

prompt: By pooling their harvests into cooperatives, independent coffee growers can negotiate directly with international roasters rather than depend on local intermediaries who pay far below market rates. question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

prompt: Data sets of plants' solar-induced chlorophyll fluorescence (a photosynthesis by-product) are derived from remote-sensor input that is highly sensitive to the first signs of photosynthesis decline, allowing scientists to detect ecosystem-wide plant stress caused by drought when such stress is __________ and not yet reflected in vegetation indices, like the Normalized Difference Vegetation Index.
question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
explanation: 'Incipient' (mới chớm nở, mới bắt đầu xuất hiện) tương ứng với 'the first signs' và việc chỉ số thực vật chưa kịp ghi nhận.

prompt: In her first project, Karunaratne House (1947–1951), architect Minnette de Silva fused modern design with traditional Sri Lankan arts and crafts. prompt: Some of the islands settled by ancient Polynesian voyagers offered fertile volcanic soil and abundant fresh water, whereas others were low-lying coral atolls with thin soil and scarce fresh water that could be reached only after weeks of open-ocean sailing. prompt: In 1927, physicist Thomas Parnell of the University of Queensland in Australia heated a sample of pitch—a tar derivative that appears solid at room temperature and can shatter when struck with a hammer—and poured it into a glass funnel with a sealed stem. question: Which choice best states the main purpose of the text?

options.A: To explain why a substance that appears solid can shatter when struck

prompt: Pointing to Scandinavian countries, where citizens report high levels of confidence in one another, some political scientists hold that widespread social trust enables governments to build effective, impartial institutions. prompt:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Archaeological sites in the Serrana Valley contain pottery in several distinct styles from different periods.
• Cordmarked ware (4,800–4,200 years ago) features surfaces impressed with twisted cords.
• Redslip ware (4,000–3,500 years ago) features polished red surfaces and incised geometric designs.
• Painted Spiral ware (from 2,600 years ago onward) features black spiral motifs painted on a cream background.
• A 2024 excavation led by Tomás Ferreira et al. identified 140 sherds of a previously unrecognized style with plain gray surfaces and a single band of stamped dots near the rim.
• The excavation's stratigraphic analysis showed that these 'Banded Gray' sherds consistently lie in layers above Redslip ware and below Painted Spiral ware.
question: The student wants to make and support a claim about the Banded Gray style based on Ferreira et al.'s excavation. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

options.A: The Banded Gray style likely represents a transition between the cord-impressed surfaces of Cordmarked ware and the polished surfaces of Redslip ware.
options.B: Ferreira et al.'s excavation proved that pottery in the Serrana Valley became steadily more decorated over time, as the Banded Gray sherds show.
options.C: The Banded Gray style should be considered the most technically sophisticated pottery in the Serrana Valley, since its stamped dots required specialized tools.
options.D: Because its sherds consistently lie above Redslip ware and below Painted Spiral ware, the Banded Gray style likely dates to the period between about 3,500 and 2,600 years ago.

explanation: Dựa trên phân tích địa tầng (nằm giữa lớp đồ gốm Redslip 3,500 năm trước và đồ gốm Painted Spiral 2,600 năm trước), phương án D đưa ra kết luận chuẩn xác về niên đại của phong cách Banded Gray.
